trigger: any BatchHeartbeat batch with an over-length id not held by this replica
summary: record_directory_desync logged 'guard rejected the write ... directory may be out of sync' for the new batch_heartbeat/malformed_session_id outcome although no write is attempted; reported independently by security-guardian, sre, docs-writer and architect (consistency-auditor read it as consistent with malformed_home_id).
classification_rationale: the log text contradicts the HELP text and the code path (no write is attempted)

trigger: debug logging off, batch where most entries are unknown (post-restart)
summary: hb.session_id().substr(0, 64) allocates a temporary std::string per unknown entry before spdlog decides whether debug is enabled; cpp-expert reported the same.
classification_rationale: performance nit, no behavioural contradiction

trigger: a session registers or is erased between the first-loop lookup and the store-block lookup
summary: A comment claimed a single source of truth for the unknown set; the set is a first-loop snapshot not atomic with the store block, so an id that registers in between is renewed AND listed/counted unknown, and one erased in between is acked but neither renewed nor counted. Reported by architect, cpp-safety and cpp-expert.
classification_rationale: the comment contradicts the two-lookup code

trigger: one batch of many distinct short unknown ids at the 4 MiB gRPC default receive limit
summary: The unknown set grows before any cap (bounded only by the receive limit, tens of MB transient worst case); the old store-block set had the same shape. Capping the stored set would saturate the unknown_session count, so the decision is to leave it uncapped and document the bound. Reported by cpp-safety and security-guardian.
classification_rationale: no comment stated the bound or the reason

trigger: one authenticated agent flooding up to 10000 distinct junk ids per batch (the gateway queues heartbeats verbatim)
summary: The claim that omitted ids are reported again at the next heartbeat is false under a junk-id flood: a legitimate id is listed with probability about 4096/J per batch and the unordered_set order is deterministic for a stable junk set, so starvation can persist. unhappy-path additionally listed I3 for the false claim; the recorder derives I8 for the doc claim and I6 for the repair gap. The behaviour itself belongs to the gateway-side replay; this change softens the claim everywhere it is stated.
classification_rationale: the doc/proto/comment claim does not hold under the flood scenario

trigger: an operator reads the compat row
summary: 'now count there' pointed at the old series; the ids now count under batch_heartbeat/malformed_session_id; the row also said 'no behaviour change' while describing a relabel. Reported by docs-writer, architect and consistency-auditor.
classification_rationale: the sentence contradicts the code

trigger: an operator reads the HELP text or metrics.md
summary: HELP and metrics.md attributed a sustained malformed_session_id rate to a 'buggy or hostile gateway'; an agent can supply the over-length id because the gateway queues heartbeats verbatim. Reported by docs-writer, security-guardian and compliance-officer.
classification_rationale: the attribution contradicts the verbatim-queue behaviour

trigger: an operator or auditor reads the ADR note as availability assurance
summary: The ADR note stated inferred dynamics as fact: 'never recovered', the directory-fallback mechanism, 'converges in one round', 'correct and bounded', and cited rig evidence kept only in a scratch directory. Reported by docs-writer, compliance-officer, architect and enterprise-readiness.
classification_rationale: claims stronger than the observed or read evidence

trigger: an operator or implementer reads repo text
summary: Internal labels (D23, D25, PR-B, PR-C, advice-1197) and 'tied to the 10000 buffer' appeared in repo comments and docs; the constant is deliberately smaller than the buffer bound. Reported by docs-writer and enterprise-readiness.
classification_rationale: wording only

summary: The outcome-specific warn lives as a string-keyed branch inside the shared record_directory_desync; a metric-only increment split from the log (or a DesyncKind parameter) is the cleaner seam.
classification_rationale: design preference, behaviour correct

trigger: a batch with more than 4096 distinct unknown ids
summary: Truncation has only a spdlog warn, no counter. Reported by sre and security-guardian; architect and sre agree it belongs with the gateway-side replay, where truncation becomes a convergence-delay signal.
classification_rationale: observability gap on an inert list

trigger: the gateway-side replay (not built) acting on a stale, disconnected or flood-influenced verdict
summary: Obligations for the gateway-side replay raised by unhappy-path UP-2..UP-7 and UP-10: replay only ids seen in at least two batches, check local liveness at replay time (no ghost resurrection), dedupe against replay_queue and reuse the drip pacing, suppress replays while the directory is unavailable and exclude them from breaker accounting, a 'verdict ever seen' gauge for version skew, sanitise ids before logging in Erlang. Inert today; tracked in #1197.
classification_rationale: the consumer is not part of this change
